title.narrative: Output 5.3. Increased capacity of Member States to design and deliver innovative, flexible and inclusive learning options, encompassing work-based learning and quality apprenticeships

description.narrative: In July 2023 a National Apprenticeship Policy (NAP) was developed by a National Apprenticeship Taskforce which was installed in 2022. The Taskforce is a tripartite sub-committee of The Bahamas Cabinet. The Bahamas is recovering from the impacts of the pandemic and Hurricane Dorian, that led to a high unemployment rate among youth (15-24 years old), and particularly among young females. Current Bahamian economic growth prospects are on an upward trajectory. The National Apprenticeship Policy provides guidance for the implementation of a quality apprenticeship system for young Bahamians to acquire the at-school and on-the-job skills, while placed as apprentices within local employers, and benefit from this trajectory. This result corresponds with Output 1.2, Indicator 1.2.1 of the Decent Work Country Programme (DWCP) for The Bahamas (2021 – 2026). Between April 2023 and July 2023, the ILO facilitated the development of ; the National Apprenticeship Policy, by providing capacity building on the Quality Apprenticeship Standard, adopted at the 111 ILC, and technical advice for the development of the policy according to the principles of this standard.
